missions.title: Starting snapshot
missions.body: Don't try to change anything today. Just log your urges and behaviours in your diary; seeing where you stand is the first step.

missions.title: Trigger hunt
missions.body: Today, when an urge comes, notice what happened just before: the place, the time, the feeling. Write one sentence in your diary.

missions.title: Your value sentence
missions.body: Choose one of the value cards and complete this sentence: “The small step I'll take this week in line with this value: …”

missions.title: Before and after
missions.body: If a behaviour happened, compare the feeling before and after it. If not, write what you felt during an urge moment.

missions.title: First friction
missions.body: Tonight, charge your phone outside the bedroom. A small obstacle slows down an automatic behaviour.

missions.title: HALT check
missions.body: Ask yourself three times during the day: am I hungry, angry, lonely or tired? Note your answer.

missions.title: First week's summary
missions.body: Look at the weekly summary in your diary. Which is your riskiest hour? Choose an If–Then plan for that hour.

missions.title: Your phone's own filter
missions.body: Set up your phone's own filter from the Environment and digital boundaries screen (Screen Time on iPhone, Digital Wellbeing on Android).

missions.title: Night rule
missions.body: Turn off screens 30 minutes before bed. Put a book, music or a calm conversation in their place.

missions.title: Home screen layout
missions.body: Remove trigger apps from your home screen or move them into a folder. An extra few seconds becomes a brake.

missions.title: Risky-hour plan
missions.body: Write two alternative activities for your riskiest time range: a walk, a shower, calling someone, a breathing session…

missions.title: Greyscale
missions.body: Tonight, switch your screen to greyscale and notice how the screen feels to you.

missions.title: Your supporter
missions.body: Without giving details, tell someone you trust that you might message them in hard moments. Saying “Sometimes I might need to talk” is enough.

missions.title: Boundary check
missions.body: Which of the boundaries you set this week worked? Make one of them a little stronger.

missions.title: First wave
missions.body: When an urge comes, watch it like a wave: notice it rise, peak and fall. If you like, do it together with the breathing on the Urge moment screen.

missions.title: Name the thought
missions.body: When a thought like “Just once won't hurt” comes, say to yourself: “Right now I'm noticing the thought that …”

missions.title: Breathing practice
missions.body: Do two minutes of breathing exercise when there's no urge. A skill practised in calm moments is easier to remember in hard ones.

missions.title: Make room
missions.body: Watch an uncomfortable feeling for 60 seconds without trying to change it. Where is it in your body, and what does it feel like?

missions.title: New paths list
missions.body: List three new things you can do in stressful or difficult moments.

missions.title: Your self-compassion sentence
missions.body: Write a kind sentence you'll say to yourself in a hard moment. What would you say to a friend?

missions.title: Tool review
missions.body: Look at the weekly summary in your diary: which tool helped most? Get it ready for the next hard moment.

missions.title: Riding the wave with movement
missions.body: During an urge moment, try the 2-minute movement set and note how you feel afterwards.

missions.title: Future me
missions.body: Write yourself a short letter in the “Future me” section of the Urge moment screen.

missions.title: What the feeling needs
missions.body: Which feeling came before the urge today? What did that feeling need, and how else could you take care of it?

missions.title: Ten minutes
missions.body: During an urge moment, put off your decision for 10 minutes and watch how the urge changes.

missions.title: Kind inner voice
missions.body: Notice a harsh sentence in your self-talk and replace it with a kinder one.

missions.title: Your favourite skill
missions.body: Today, consciously use the skill that has helped you most so far.

missions.title: Skills week
missions.body: What have you learned in these two weeks? Write it in one sentence.

missions.title: Bedtime
missions.body: This week, try going to bed at the same time every day. Regular sleep can ease urges that come at night.

missions.title: Night routine
missions.body: Create a calm three-step routine before bed: turn off the screen, dim the light, a few minutes of breathing or reading.

missions.title: Connection plan
missions.body: Make a plan to meet a friend or a family member this week.

missions.title: A new pastime
missions.body: Spend 20 minutes on a hobby you're curious about: drawing, music, cooking, a language…

missions.title: Time to move
missions.body: Go for a 20-minute walk or do a fitness session in the app.

missions.title: Take care of your body
missions.body: Give your body a few minutes with a Kegel or breathing session in the app.

missions.title: Weekly connection task
missions.body: Join a community activity or call someone you haven't talked to in a long time.

missions.title: Instead of the screen
missions.body: During your risky hour, do the alternative activity you planned.

missions.title: Meaning
missions.body: Write three things you did this week in line with your values.

missions.title: Sleep check
missions.body: Look at your daily checks: has your sleep quality changed?

missions.title: A respectful view
missions.body: Read the “Healthy view of sexuality” lesson and write a principle that suits you.

missions.title: Thank you
missions.body: Thank someone who has supported you through this.

missions.title: Routine check
missions.body: Which new routine has done you the most good? Plan to keep it up in the coming weeks.

missions.title: End of the core programme
missions.body: You've completed six weeks. Redo the short screening and look at your own progress; it's not a grade, just a snapshot.

missions.title: High-risk situations map
missions.body: Read the “Relapse prevention plan” lesson and make a plan for your three riskiest situations.

missions.title: Early warning signs
missions.body: Write three signs you usually notice before a slip (e.g. poor sleep, loneliness, late-night phone use).

missions.title: Your identity sentence
missions.body: Write the sentence “I'm someone who lives by my values” in your own words.

missions.title: Update your plans
missions.body: Update one of your If–Then plans to fit your life today.

missions.title: Keep connecting
missions.body: Spend face-to-face time with someone this week.

missions.title: Thank yourself
missions.body: Write three things you thank yourself for in this process.

missions.title: Maintenance plan
missions.body: Day 90 is close. Prepare a small monthly check plan for the months ahead.

missions.title: 90 days
missions.body: You've completed 90 days. Redo the short screening and look back on your journey. From now on, a monthly check is enough.
